parameters.content:
## Trellis Static Ad — v1.3

Generates ONE publish-ready static ad image + copy. The image is generated completely clean of text — the Trellis app composites the headline onto it afterward in the real brand font (`branches.font_family`) using the brand's actual hex colours. A self-check pass (Vision QA) confirms the image came back text-free before it reaches approval.

**In:** POST /webhook/trellis-static-ad-generate
```
{ job_id, branch, message,
  target_segment, platform,
  aspect_ratio, setting, style_notes,
  reference_image_url?, reference_mode?,
  revision_of?, revision_notes? }
```
`reference_image_url` (optional): a public URL of a real photo.
`reference_mode`: 'edit' = keep the photo exactly as shot, generated clean of any added text; 'inspire' (default) = generate a new image guided by the photo's setting/mood/composition, also clean of text.
`revision_of` (optional): UUID of a prior job being regenerated. `revision_notes` (optional): free-text feedback on why the prior attempt was rejected - it is appended to both the copy prompt and the image prompt. The app resubmits the SAME original body plus these two fields; the job row's `request_payload` (saved by Upsert Job Record) is what makes that replay possible.
**Out:** job row -> status `awaiting_approval`, with `frame_url`, `media_urls` (1 item), `caption`, `frame_prompt` set. The image has NO AI-drawn text on it — headline compositing happens client-side in the Trellis app.

Approval + publish happen in the Trellis app (Video Ad Lab), which hands off to the existing B3 social publisher webhook (`trellis-social-publish`) with `media_type: 'image'`.

### v1.3: real brand colours + clean imagery
Brand colours were never reaching the model — `brand_profiles.brand_colors` is `[]` for every brand, so prompts fell back to generic "Colour palette consistent with X" phrasing. **Lookup Branch Style** (new node, reuses the same Supabase credential — no new setup) now reads `branches` directly for `primary_color` / `secondary_color` / `accent_color` (and `font_family`), matching on `branches.slug = body.branch` — a clean equality match against the bare slug the app already sends, unlike `Lookup Brand Profile`'s prefix hack against `brand_profiles.branch`. `Prepare Copy Prompt` reads it defensively and passes `primary`/`secondary`/`accent` forward through the node chain into the image prompt; `Parse Copy` falls back to brand-name phrasing only when no hex colours are on file.
Separately, this workflow no longer asks the model to draw the headline onto the image at all. Every image prompt now reserves generous negative space (lower third) for text and carries a hard "no text of any kind" negative clause. **Vision QA no longer checks legibility — it checks that the image is free of text**, and retries once if any text shows up. The app is responsible for compositing the real headline, in the real brand font and colours, after generation.

### Setup
1. Credentials — reuse the same 3 as Trellis-Video-Ad-Frame-v1 (Lookup Branch Style reuses the Supabase one, no new credential needed):
   • **Sproutify Trellis** (Supabase) — id `IkIpi5m4OmJ9DvBS`
   • **Gemini API** (Query Auth) — replace `REPLACE_GEMINI_CRED`
   • **Supabase Storage (legacy eyJ service role)** (Header Auth) — replace `REPLACE_SUPABASE_STORAGE_CRED`
2. Prerequisite SQL (Hub, run once — idempotent):
```sql
ALTER TABLE video_ad_jobs ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS format TEXT;
ALTER TABLE video_ad_jobs ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS media_urls JSONB DEFAULT '[]';
ALTER TABLE video_ad_jobs ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS caption TEXT;
ALTER TABLE video_ad_jobs ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS request_payload JSONB;
ALTER TABLE video_ad_jobs ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS revision_of UUID;
ALTER TABLE video_ad_jobs ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS revision_notes TEXT;
```
(`request_payload` / `revision_of` / `revision_notes` are already applied to the live Hub DB - this SQL is for the record / fresh environments.)
3. Activate, then point the Video Ad Lab's static-ad action at `https://n8n.sproutify.app/webhook/trellis-static-ad-generate`.

This workflow STOPS at `awaiting_approval`. It does not publish anything.

### Why copy still comes before the image
The headline/caption still need to exist before the image request goes out. Nano Banana no longer draws the headline onto the picture, but `Parse Copy` still uses the brand tone, setting and (as of v1.3) the real `primary`/`secondary`/`accent` hex colours from `Lookup Branch Style` to build the image prompt, and the app needs the headline text available for client-side compositing regardless. So **Generate Copy** still runs first and **Parse Copy** still builds the final image prompt.

### Why the QA loop
Nano Banana sometimes ignores the "no text" instruction and draws letters, watermarks or logos anyway. **Vision QA** re-reads its own output and now checks for the ABSENCE of any text; if text is detected it retries **once** with a stronger no-text prompt (`Track Frame Attempt` uses `$runIndex` the same way F1's poll loop does), then proceeds regardless so the job never stalls — a human approves it either way. The image must be clean because the Trellis app composites the real headline on top of it afterward, in the real brand font and colours.

nodes.name: Upsert Job Record
nodes.notes: Insert on first run. On a resubmit the row already exists and this 409s harmlessly - onError lets it pass through, mirrors Trellis-Video-Ad-Frame-v1. request_payload persists the exact inbound body (via JSON.stringify) so the app's 'Regenerate' button can replay it unchanged with revision_of/revision_notes added on top. Like media_urls elsewhere in this workflow, confirm on first run that Supabase writes it as real jsonb and not a double-encoded string - documented fallback is a raw HTTP PATCH node with Content-Type: application/json instead of this Supabase node field. CONFIRMED on live runs: PostgREST stores this JSON.stringify'd value as a jsonb *string*, not a native array/object (jsonb_typeof = 'string'). The app normalizes it on read via parseJsonbField() in services/videoAdService.ts. Do NOT remove the JSON.stringify without updating that normalizer - and note jsonb_array_length / the GIN index cannot be used while it is stored this way.

nodes.name: Lookup Brand Profile
nodes.notes: Prefix match so both bare slugs and domain keys in brand_profiles resolve. If nothing matches, downstream falls back to branch name + 'friendly' tone. Colour values now come from Lookup Branch Style (branches table) instead - brand_profiles.brand_colors is unused.

nodes.name: Lookup Branch Style
nodes.notes: Exact slug match against branches.slug - the app sends the bare slug (e.g. atlurbanfarms), which matches this column exactly, unlike Lookup Brand Profile's prefix hack against brand_profiles.branch. Supplies primary_color / secondary_color / accent_color (and font_family) for the real brand colours; brand_profiles.brand_colors is empty for every brand, so this is the only source of truth for hex values used in image prompts.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ contents: [{ parts: [{ text: $('Prepare Copy Prompt').item.json.copy_prompt }] }], generationConfig: { temperature: 0.8, maxOutputTokens: 2048, responseMimeType: 'application/json', responseSchema: { type: 'OBJECT', properties: { headline: { type: 'STRING' }, subtext: { type: 'STRING' }, cta: { type: 'STRING' }, caption: { type: 'STRING' } }, required: ['headline','subtext','cta','caption'] } } }) }}

nodes.name: Generate Copy
nodes.notes: gemini-flash-latest with responseMimeType application/json + responseSchema, so the API itself guarantees parseable JSON. Prose-asking for JSON previously let the model return a markdown explanation of the schema, which then got rendered onto the image as the headline. maxOutputTokens is generous because thinking tokens count against the budget and a truncated response is unparseable.

nodes.name: Parse Copy
nodes.notes: Gemini now returns schema-enforced JSON, so parsing normally succeeds. The fallback exists for transport failures and rejects junk headlines (markdown, field names, 'max 8 words') so they never reach the app's text-compositing step - which is exactly what happened on the first live run. As of v1.3 the image prompt is built completely clean of any headline-rendering instruction - it reserves negative space and forbids text outright. Text is composited by the Trellis app afterward using branches.font_family and the real brand hex colours (primary/secondary/accent) looked up via Lookup Branch Style.

nodes.name: Track Frame Attempt
nodes.notes: $runIndex is this node's own execution count within the workflow run - same idiom F1 uses in 'Bump Progress'. attempt=1 first pass, attempt=2 on the single retry.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ contents: [{ parts: (($json.ref_base64) ? [{ text: $json.image_prompt + ($json.attempt > 1 ? ' Regenerate this image with absolutely NO text, letters, words, numbers, logos, watermarks or captions anywhere in the frame - the previous attempt contained unwanted text that must not appear this time.' : '') }, { inlineData: { mimeType: $json.ref_mime, data: $json.ref_base64 } }] : [{ text: $json.image_prompt + ($json.attempt > 1 ? ' Regenerate this image with absolutely NO text, letters, words, numbers, logos, watermarks or captions anywhere in the frame - the previous attempt contained unwanted text that must not appear this time.' : '') }]) }], generationConfig: { responseModalities: ['IMAGE'], imageConfig: { aspectRatio: $json.aspect_ratio } } }) }}

nodes.name: Generate Image
nodes.notes: Nano Banana 2 (gemini-3.1-flash-image). Returns inlineData base64 in candidates[].content.parts[]. When ref_base64 is present (reference photo), it is attached as a second inlineData part - 'edit' mode keeps the photo without drawing any text onto it, 'inspire' mode generates a fresh, clean image. As of v1.3, every mode forbids on-image text - the Trellis app composites the real headline afterward in the real brand font and colours.

nodes.name: Extract Image
nodes.notes: Keeps base64 in json (not just binary) so Vision QA downstream can reuse it without a re-download step.

nodes.name: Upload Image to Storage
nodes.notes: Same episode-assets bucket as Trellis-Video-Ad-Frame-v1, under a static-ads/ prefix. MUST use the legacy eyJ... JWT service role key - upsert:false + a randomised filename avoids the UPDATE RLS policy on Storage, same as Frame v1.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ contents: [{ parts: [{ text: 'You are a quality checker for a marketing static ad image that must come back completely free of text, because the headline is composited onto it separately afterward by the app. Look closely at the attached image. Does it contain ANY text, letters, words, numbers, logos, watermarks, signage or captions of any kind? Reply with exactly one line: the single word YES if the image is completely free of text/letters/words/logos/watermarks, or the word NO followed by a short reason if any appear.' }, { inlineData: { mimeType: $('Extract Image').item.json.mime, data: $('Extract Image').item.json.base64 } }] }], generationConfig: { temperature: 0, maxOutputTokens: 200 } }) }}

nodes.name: Vision QA
nodes.notes: One multimodal Gemini call reading back its own generated image. gemini-flash-latest is multimodal, so no new model id is introduced. As of v1.3 this checks for the ABSENCE of text - the workflow no longer draws headline text onto the image, so any text appearing here is unwanted AI noise (the model ignoring the no-text instruction), not a rendering-quality issue.

nodes.name: Parse QA Result
nodes.notes: passed=true now means Vision QA confirmed the image is text-free (v1.3). Before v1.3, YES meant the on-image headline text was legible - the meaning of the underlying question flipped when this workflow switched to app-composited text, but the regex (/^\s*yes/i) and the downstream QA Passed? / retry wiring are unchanged.

nodes.name: QA Passed?
nodes.notes: True when QA said YES, OR we've already used our one retry (attempt >= 2) - proceeds either way so the job never stalls. False loops back to Track Frame Attempt exactly once.

nodes.name: Update: Awaiting Approval
nodes.notes: Terminal state for this workflow. media_urls is written as a JSON.stringify'd array via the Supabase node - after first run, confirm in the table editor that the column stores a real JSON array and not a double-encoded string; if PostgREST stores it as a scalar string, switch this field to a raw HTTP PATCH node with Content-Type: application/json instead. CONFIRMED on live runs: PostgREST stores this JSON.stringify'd value as a jsonb *string*, not a native array/object (jsonb_typeof = 'string'). The app normalizes it on read via parseJsonbField() in services/videoAdService.ts. Do NOT remove the JSON.stringify without updating that normalizer - and note jsonb_array_length / the GIN index cannot be used while it is stored this way.

nodes.name: Has Reference?
nodes.notes: True -> fetch the user's reference photo and attach it to the Nano Banana request. False -> plain text-to-image, exactly as v1.0 behaved.

nodes.name: Fetch Reference Image
nodes.notes: Downloads the reference photo (public URL from the Trellis app's upload, avatars bucket). No auth needed.

nodes.name: Reference to Base64
nodes.notes: getBinaryDataBuffer is the safe way to read binary regardless of n8n's binary-data storage mode. Merges the Track Frame Attempt fields forward so Generate Image sees one flat json either way.
